title: ACP Surface Audit v1

current_state.summary: RigACPAgent implements ACP models: sessions, progress events, edit proposals, permission requests, terminal output, plans. Models are well-designed with content-light guards (touched_path_hashes, diff_sha256, output_sha256). No transport server exists. Entrypoint (rig_relay/cli/acp_entrypoint.py) delegates to legacy vibe.*. IDE sidecar runs ACP agent on separate asyncio task but ACP transport is not integrated. ACP capability profile shows authenticate_supported=false, resume_supported=false, content_light=true.
current_state.maturity: partial — models implemented, agent class skeleton exists, no transport server, no session persistence, no integration with mission system

acp_role_recommendation.primary_role: Rig Relay should act as an ACP server (agent) that editors can drive. It should NOT act as an ACP client consuming other agents — that role belongs to the orchestrator via A2A.
acp_role_recommendation.secondary_role: ACP may also serve as a client for consuming editor context (workspace snapshot, selection, diagnostics) to enrich agent context. This is already partially done via IDE sidecar.
acp_role_recommendation.not_recommended: ACP as a peer-to-peer agent communication protocol — that's A2A's job. ACP as a replacement for MCP tool access — MCP is better suited for tools/resources/prompts; ACP is for session-oriented coding agent interaction.

allowed: edit proposals (content-light, diff_sha256, never direct write)
forbidden: direct file write without edit proposal + approval
raw file content in progress events
raw diff content outside edit proposals
bypass of mission scope or governance gates

how_acp_differs_from_mcp.mcp_purpose: Tool/resource/prompt access for AI clients. Stateless request/response over JSON-RPC. Good for: search evidence, read receipts, run validators, propose patches.
how_acp_differs_from_mcp.acp_purpose: Session-oriented coding agent interaction for editor integration. Stateful sessions with progress streaming, edit proposals, permission requests. Good for: IDE-driven missions, progress tracking, interactive code editing with human review.
how_acp_differs_from_mcp.acp_vs_a2a: ACP is for human-in-the-loop editor-agent interaction. A2A is for agent-to-agent delegation across trust boundaries. ACP sessions involve human approval. A2A delegations involve agent trust tiers.

acp_design_requirements: ACP transport must be separate from MCP transport — different concerns, different auth models
ACP sessions must persist to coordination store — session state must survive restart
ACP must integrate with mission system — ACP sessions map to Rig missions
ACP edit proposals must produce patch_proposal artifacts in the same format as MCP rig.propose_patch
ACP permission requests must flow through GovernanceEngine — same path as cockpit intents
ACP terminal output must use RuntimeSupervisor — same subprocess supervision as local tool execution
ACP must NOT bypass cockpit approval for mutations — if cockpit is active, ACP requests should queue for cockpit review
ACP resume must be supported — sessions must be resumable from coordination store
ACP must produce receipts for every message category — session receipts, proposal receipts, permission receipts, terminal receipts

ide_sidecar_convergence.current: IDE sidecar bridges VSCodium extension with ACP agent over stdin/stdout JSONL. 42 capabilities with per-capability risk and policy. Capability manifest is single authority.
ide_sidecar_convergence.convergence_path: IDE sidecar should become the primary ACP transport implementation. Currently sidecar uses its own IPC protocol. Should converge to standard ACP message format so other editors (JetBrains, Zed) can use the same ACP transport.

acp_tests_required: test_acp_edit_proposal_never_direct_write — sabotage: attempt direct write via ACP, verify blocked
test_acp_permission_request_flows_through_governance — contract: permission request evaluated by GovernanceEngine
test_acp_terminal_output_uses_runtime_supervisor — contract: terminal command executed via RuntimeSupervisor
test_acp_cannot_bypass_cockpit_approval — integration: cockpit active, ACP mutation requests queued
test_acp_message_schema_validation — contract: invalid ACP messages rejected
test_acp_resume_session — contract: resumed session has correct state
